text:
anita: heads-up — canary 'canary-2026-03' error rate jumped to ~6% over the last 3m, guard fired. starting a single thread to coordinate a fast but safe unwind.

juan: where are the current splits? console still shows 10% -> canary, trying to push split to 0% but it’s idempotent-hanging.

deploy-bot: [auto] routing-guard: error_rate > 5% for route `/api/v1/generate` (3m window). new canaries paused, not allowing traffic increases.

tom: proposed immediate plan: 1) stop any ongoing traffic shift jobs; 2) shift traffic back to stable variant; 3) annotate rollout as failed; 4) targeted KV sweep for session keys older than 30m only. keep it minimal to avoid cold-cache shock.

maya: +1 but do NOT full-purge caches. use prefix sweep with min-age and grace. evicting all sess: keys will spike downstream DB calls.

anita: commands i'm going to run (dry-run first):
```bash
# flip traffic back to stable (gradual if affinity needed)
redwood rollout update --id r-845 --split stable=98,canary=2 --reason "auto-revert:guard"
# mark canary status in rollout metadata
redwood rollout annotate --id r-845 --set canary_status=failed --note "auto-guard triggered"
# KV sweep dry-run then execute
redwood kv sweep --prefix "sess:" --min-age 1800 --dry-run
redwood kv sweep --prefix "sess:" --min-age 1800 --execute --grace 120
```

juan: telemetry ask: can someone snapshot per-route latencies, 5xx rate, and token-cost for last 30m and attach to incident? we need it for postmortem.

tom: on it. running a quick query for traces + route-level CPU/GPU mem + token billing delta. also flagging service quotas — stable might need a temporary burst raise if we move 100% traffic back.

maya: important: preserve session-affinity header `x-rw-session` if possible. if affinity can't be honoured when we cut canary to 0, we should drain canary nodes instead of instant cutover (avoid 400/5xx for in-flight sessions).

anita: short rollback checklist for the thread (copy to runbook):
- pause rollout jobs / disable any pending traffic-change automations
- disable autoscaler on canary pool (prevent scale-down races)
- set rollout split stable=100, canary=0 OR 98/2 then drain (depending on affinity)
- if errors persist, set routing mode to safe-disable: `redwood routing set --mode safe-disable --reason "rollback"`
- targeted KV sweep (prefix + min-age) 
- monitor telemetry dashboards (rollout-health, per-route-errors, quota-usage) for 15m after change
- annotate rollout + incident with commit/PR that caused rollout
- only re-open canary after patch + bake period + approval

juan: question — when we flip to safe-disable, does that also disable per-route caching? I thought safe-disable only prevents routing to canary.

tom: safe-disable blocks routing decisions to the failing variant and prevents new canary allocations. it does NOT globally flush caches, but it may bypass prefix-based canary cache keys. must be explicit about kv sweeps.

maya: add to runbook: include these artifact snapshots in incident: rollout_id, rollout diff, console split history, per-route cache hit-rate, kv hit/miss histogram, and a small sample of failed payloads.

deploy-bot: [action] creating incident INC-2026-0423 and attaching current guard log + recent traces.

anita: i'm going to execute the split update now (dry-run then execute). tagging @oncall to watch the rollout-health dashboard. :eyes:

juan: ack — i'll monitor quota counters (burst tokens, per-route concurrency). if throttles spike i'll open rapid-revert and we can flip stable->previous-binary.

tom: post-update acceptance criteria: 5xx < 1% for 10m AND token-cost delta within expected bounds. if either fails, trigger full revert to previously pinned model binary and follow postmortem.

maya: after we've stabilized, we need a short follow-up: update the rollout UX to expose an explicit 'evacuate-canary' action that does affinity-aware drain + kv-sweep dry-run. reduces manual steps next time.

anita: agreed. logging steps and notes to the runbook now. will paste dry-run outputs into the incident thread.

juan: thanks all — moving to watch mode.
